subject: Clarifying cost model: tokens vs characters vs requests + caching impact
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Green <sasha@quickatlas.com>, Andre Muller <andre.muller@quickatlas.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 15:00:00 -0400
Subject: QuickAtlas - post-demo cost model recap and next steps

Hi Sasha / Andre,

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation and useful context on where QuickAtlas wants to deploy summarization + RAG for customer support. Per our ask: below is a concise recap of the cost/pricing items we discussed and concrete next steps so procurement has something actionable.

1) Pricing metrics — definitions (short)
- Token: Redwood bills by token for generation/transform operations. Tokens are model-tokenizer units (approx ¾ of an English word on average).
- Character: not used for billing on Redwood; sometimes customers map chars -> tokens internally (useful for estimation).
- Request: an API call. You can reduce requests with batching or multi-turn session approaches.

2) Prompt caching vs billed tokens — the key point
- Prompt caching stores KV cache/response for repeated prompts to avoid running the full model.
- If a request is served entirely from a cache hit at the routing layer, your billed tokens for that request can be materially lower (you may still pay a small lookup/runtime fee depending on config).
- Put simply: cache hits reduce billed model tokens; requests still count toward throughput but are cheaper per-op.

3) Worked example (for clarity)
- Typical call: 600-token prompt (user + system) -> model returns 1,800 tokens. Total billed = 2,400 tokens.
- With prefix cache hit on the 600-token prompt and a cached response chunk of 1,200 tokens, a repeat call might only bill ~600 tokens (depending on exact cache policy and response reuse).
- Target cost we discussed: you mentioned wanting ~ $300–500 / 1M tokens as an internal budget target. Based on that, estimate monthly spend by multiplying expected monthly billed tokens (after cache) by unit price.

4) Estimation asks for us to push a formal quote
- Can you confirm expected monthly "billed" token volume (not raw characters) after accounting for expected cache hit rate? Example options: 50M, 200M, 1B.
- Your procurement requested a target per-1M-token price. We can propose tiered pricing for 100M+ and 500M+ commitments.

5) Next steps
- I attached a brief pricing cheatsheet and a draft SOW for your procurement team.
- If you can reply with (A) expected monthly billed tokens after cache and (B) desired contract term (12/24 months), I’ll pull together a committed pricing option + formal SOW.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-pricing-cheatsheet.xlsx (xlsx)], [Attachment: QuickAtlas_SOW_draft_v1.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min follow-up if helpful.

Best,

From: Sasha Green <sasha@quickatlas.com>

Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 17:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: QuickAtlas - post-demo cost model recap and next steps

Hi Grace — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions before we give procurement a numbers target: 

1) When you say "billed tokens" is that always prompt + completion, or are there cases where we only pay for the completion? For example, if we store a canonical prompt and only supply a 1–2 sentence delta at request time, do we get billed for the full prompt?

2) Cache behavior: if we use a hybrid approach (partial response reuse + live completion), how do you meter that? Our use case will have a high degree of repeated system prompts but slightly varied user text.

3) Internationalization: we do a lot of Spanish & German support; tokenization density differs. Should procurement give you characters rather than guessed tokens to estimate?

4) Also: for the tiered pricing, what are the typical $/1M-token midpoints at 100M, 500M, and 1B committed buckets? A ballpark range is fine — procurement just needs to know if our $300–500 target is plausible for our expected volumes.

(Quoted text)

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 18:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: QuickAtlas - post-demo cost model recap and next steps

Thanks Sasha — good questions. Short answers up front, then a couple of numbers.

1) Billed tokens: usually prompt + completion. However, with explicit prefix caching and deterministic response reuse we can avoid re-running the full prompt model path; in that case you are billed significantly fewer model tokens for that request. Practically: think of billing as "what the model actually executed". If the model is skipped because a cached response/kv-lookup suffices, your billed tokens drop accordingly.

2) Partial reuse: we meter at the model-execution granularity. If a partial response is reused and only the tail is generated live (e.g., first 1,200 tokens cached, last 300 generated), billed tokens are the generated tail + any low-cost routing overhead. We can provide a sample log extract showing exact billed token counts per request if that helps procurement reconcile invoices.

3) Internationalization: yes, token per char density varies. When procurement prefers character counts we convert using an average conversion factor per language (we typically use 0.75 token/char for English as a starting point, Spanish tends to be similar, German slightly higher). For precise budgeting, send us a character sample and we’ll return estimated tokenized counts.

4) Ballpark $/1M-token tiers (examples only — demo pricing):
- 0–100M: $700–900 / 1M tokens (on-demand hosted)
- 100M–499M: $320–420 / 1M tokens (committed discounts start to appear)
- 500M–1B+: $220–320 / 1M tokens (largest committed discounts + reserved capacity options)

So your $300–500 target is plausible at the 100M+ range with a 12–24 month commitment and some cache-optimized workload.

Attached: quick worked example sheet and the draft SOW. I’ll also ask Karthik to prepare a short log sample showing the billing breakdown for partial cache hits so procurement can see line items.

Would you be able to share an estimated monthly "billed tokens after cache" number (50M / 200M / 1B)? If not, tell us expected monthly requests + average char length and we’ll convert.

Best,
Grace

[Attachment: redwood-pricing-cheatsheet.xlsx (xlsx)]
